validated_results.title: Phenolic Extract from Extra Virgin Olive Oil Induces Different Anti-Proliferative Pathways in Human Bladder Cancer Cell Lines.
validated_results.reason: The study tested a phenolic extract from extra virgin olive oil only on human bladder cancer cell lines (RT112, J82), providing no human population evidence on olive oil intake and bladder cancer incidence.

validated_results.title: Phenolic Extract from Extra Virgin Olive Oil Induces Different Anti-Proliferative Pathways in Human Bladder Cancer Cell Lines.
validated_results.reason: Olive-derived phenolic extract was evaluated exclusively in in vitro bladder cancer cell-line experiments, which is a preclinical design with no incident cancer outcome.

validated_results.title: Polymorphisms of Antioxidant Enzymes SOD2 (rs4880) and GPX1 (rs1050450) Are Associated with Bladder Cancer Risk or Its Aggressiveness.
validated_results.reason: The analysis concerns GPX1 and SOD2 single nucleotide polymorphisms rather than any nutritional glutathione exposure, providing no population-wide glutathione intake or biomarker estimate.

validated_results.title: Polymorphisms of Antioxidant Enzymes SOD2 (rs4880) and GPX1 (rs1050450) Are Associated with Bladder Cancer Risk or Its Aggressiveness.
validated_results.reason: Urothelial bladder cancer risk is assessed for antioxidant enzyme genotypes (rs1050450, rs4880), not for a glutathione nutritional exposure.
